about.title: About Billfold
about.body: Billfold reads the credential files, the configuration and the usage logs the AI hosts leave on this machine, and nothing else. It shows which accounts each host is logged into, where your provider keys sit, and what was consumed — in tokens first, in API-equivalent dollars second. It never calls a provider, never reads the keyring, and never writes outside its own preferences.
about.pick: Pick a finding to see what it means, where it is and what you could do.

kind.tracked-secret: A key in clear sits in a file git tracks: it is in the history of the repository, and of every clone and remote.
kind.exposed-secret: A key in clear sits in a file other users of this machine can read.
kind.clear-secret: A key is stored in clear text. The file's permissions are fine, but anything running as you can read it.
kind.shared-key: The same key is used by several tools or stored in several places: rotating it means changing it everywhere, and one leak exposes all of them.
kind.expired: The stored token or session has passed its expiry; the host will ask you to log in again, or is using something else.
kind.double-credit: This host is logged in on a subscription and also sees an API key for the same provider: one of the two pays, and the host decides which.
kind.unpriced: This model is in your logs but not in the embedded price table: its tokens are counted, its dollar equivalent is not.
kind.pruning-soon: The host deletes its usage logs after a retention period; what is older than that will soon be gone from this machine.
kind.host-disagrees: The host wrote its own cost for these requests and it differs from Billfold's estimate: a different price table, a promotion, or a tier.
kind.near-limit: The last time this host wrote its rate-limit state, a window was close to full.
kind.legacy-store: This credential file belongs to an older version of the host; the current version stores its login elsewhere.
kind.no-usage-log: This host keeps no per-request token record on disk; its usage lives only in the provider's dashboard.
kind.in-keyring: This host keeps its secrets in the system keyring, where Billfold does not look. Nothing to read, nothing exposed.
